font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company analyzes all financial instruments with features of both liabilities and equity under FASB ASC Topic No. </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c4a98c0f9c305eb9ad0a'; The classification of derivative financial instruments is reassessed each reporting period. Derivative liabilities are adjusted to reflect fair value at each reporting period, with any increase or decrease in the fair value recorded in the results of operations, as a component of other income or expense as change in fair value of derivative liabilities. As of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c1af92d97c032e45d07a'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P14'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, derivative liabilities consist of contingent payment arrangements. The Company uses a probability-weighted expected return method to determine the fair value of these instruments.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Upon conversion or repayment of a debt or equity instrument in exchange for equity shares, where the embedded conversion option has been bifurcated and accounted for as a derivative liability (generally convertible debt and warrants), the Company records the equity shares at fair value on the date of conversion, relieves all related debt, derivative liabilities, and unamortized debt discounts, and recognizes a net gain or loss on debt extinguishment, if any.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Equity or liability instruments that become subject to reclassification under ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'ce08ae8c5268be0628c7'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">815</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> are reclassified at the fair value of the instrument on the reclassification date.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c263c163ec50c04829df'"><ix:nonNumeric name="sxtp:EquityClassifiedWarrantsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag594"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; text-decoration:underline; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Equity-Classified Warrants</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">As of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c7bcd8e778eedd1caaab'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P11'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, the Company accounts for all outstanding warrants to purchase common stock as equity-classified instruments based on an assessment of the warrants&#8217; specific terms and applicable authoritative guidance in ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdb856b4f4bde6d47eab'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">480</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> and ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd5e76a6a6ce96ef7c87'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">815</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">. This assessment considers whether the warrants are freestanding financial instruments pursuant to ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd481df4cd7bb454097c'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">480</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, meet the definition of a liability pursuant to ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c75d25a4963187f34a5b'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">480</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, whether the warrants meet all of the requirements for equity classification under ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c8f59ed9b1458f19f86f'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">815</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, including whether the warrants are indexed to the Company&#8217;s own common stock and whether the warrant holders could potentially require &#8220;net cash settlement&#8221; in a circumstance outside of the Company&#8217;s control, among other conditions for equity classification. This assessment, which requires the use of professional judgment, is conducted at the respective issuance dates and as of each subsequent reporting period while the warrants are outstanding.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd350ef809c535d516f7'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag595" continuedAt="ce8fe6436ba07846a99e"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; text-decoration:underline; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Revenue Recognition</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with FASB ASC Topic No. </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c1024005423a4297ddef'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">606</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, </span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> (&#8220;ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c01990ecd114b774522a'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">606</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#8221;). Revenues are recognized when control is transferred to customers in amounts that reflect the consideration the Company expects to be entitled to receive in exchange for those goods. Revenue recognition is evaluated through the following five steps: (i) identification of the contract, or contracts, with a customer; (ii) identification of the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determination of the transaction price; (iv) allocation of the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognition of revenue when or as a performance obligation is satisfied. As part of the accounting for these arrangements, the Company may be required to make significant judgments, including identifying performance obligations in the contract, estimating the amount of variable consideration to include in the transaction price and allocating the transaction price to each performance obligation.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Revenues from product sales are recorded at the net sales price, or &#8220;transaction price,&#8221; which may include estimates of variable consideration that result from product returns. The Company determines the amount of variable consideration by using either the expected value method or the most-likely-amount method. The Company includes the unconstrained amount of estimated variable consideration in the transaction price, which reflects the amount for which it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur. At the end of each subsequent reporting period, the Company re-evaluates the estimated variable consideration included in the transaction price and any related constraint, and if necessary, adjusts its estimate of the overall transaction price. Any such adjustments are recorded on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period of adjustment. Reserves are established for the estimates of variable consideration based on the amounts the Company expects to be earned or to be claimed on the related sales.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c6053e6c5f792d82acc2'"><ix:exclude><ix:exclude><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; z-index: 100;">9</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></ix:exclude></ix:exclude></div></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div></div><div class="Section_13"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'d52-b02-e2a-ceb-f6c1'"><ix:continuation id="c86adcf05621b85c306b" continuedAt="cfb50ddcd26e1e826ca1"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd350ef809c535d516f7'"><ix:continuation id="ce8fe6436ba07846a99e"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company receives the majority of its revenues from sales of its Arakoda product to resellers in the US and abroad. The Company records US commercial revenues as a receivable when our American distributor transfers shipped product to their title model for </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cfae9bd6533b6134b81a'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">60</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">P. Foreign sales to both Australia and Europe are recognized as a receivable at the point product is shipped to the distributor. Historically, the shipments to Australia and Europe were further subject to profit sharing agreements for boxes sold to customers.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">In addition to revenue from product sales, in 2025, the Company recognized research revenues associated with its contract with the United States Army Medical Material Development Activity (USAMMDA) for Arakoda supply chain upgrade support. Research revenue under this contract was recognized when the direct costs eligible for reimbursement are incurred, up to the maximum allowable amount. Our USAMMDA-funded activities were completed during the year ended December 31, 2025. Other research revenues consist of sales of clinical trial supplies, which are recognized at a point in time, and research rebates earned from the Australian Tax Authority, which are recognized over time as qualifying research activities in Australia are performed.</span></p></ix:continuation></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; Accordingly, internal research and development costs are expensed as incurred. Prepayments for research and development services are deferred and amortized over the service period as the services are provided. Advance payments for specific materials, equipment, or facilities determined to have no alternative future use are initially deferred and recognized as research and development expense when the related goods are delivered.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Certain prior period interim amounts have been reclassified for consistency with the current period presentation. These reclassifications had no material effect on the consolidated condensed results of operations and comprehensive loss, shareholders&#8217; equity, or cash flows.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c5ae9390f02706bea469'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag607"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; text-decoration:underline; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Share-Based Payments</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">On November </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cb8e4cad4e4d214394a1'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">22</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c07fc0c7362febea5ed1'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2022</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, the Company adopted the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c82523a8da0311b6da03'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2022</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> Equity Incentive Plan also referred to as (&#8220;</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c84ff39eab4b2b69d4e5'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2022</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> Plan&#8221;). The </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c77a8fd767458ed89fe9'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2022</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> Plan and related share-based awards are discussed more fully in Note </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c89592db43d1d0460416'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">10</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company accounts for share-based payments in accordance with ASC Subtopic </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cfb759d6c4e98b9f102c'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">718</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, </span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Compensation - Stock Compensation </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">(&#8220;ASC </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c28e007bf795e0cf0e4d'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">718</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#8221;). The Company measures compensation for all share-based payment awards granted to employees, directors, and nonemployees, based on the estimated fair value of the awards on the date of grant. For awards that vest based on continued service, the service-based compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period of the awards. For service vesting awards with compensation expense recognized on a straight-line basis, at no point in time does the cumulative grant date value of vested awards exceed the cumulative amount of compensation expense recognized. The grant date is determined based on the date when a mutual understanding of the key terms of the share-based awards is established. The Company accounts for forfeitures as they occur.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company estimates the fair value of all stock option awards as of the grant date by applying the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The application of this valuation model involves assumptions, including the fair value of the common stock, expected volatility, risk-free interest rate, expected dividends and the expected term of the option. Due to the lack of a public market for the Company&#8217;s common stock prior to the IPO and lack of company-specific historical implied volatility data, the Company has based its computations of expected volatility on the historical volatility of a representative group of public companies with similar characteristics of the Company, including stage of development and industry focus. The historical volatility is calculated based on a period of time commensurate with the expected term assumption. The Company generally uses the simplified method as prescribed by the SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdc65a3ad6830dc2131f'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">14</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, </span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Share-Based Payment</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, to estimate the expected term for stock options, whereby, the expected term equals the midpoint of the weighted average remaining time to vest, vesting period and the contractual term of the options due to its lack of historical exercise data. For certain options granted out-of-the-money, the Company&#8217;s best estimate of the expected term is the contractual term of the award. The risk-free interest rate is based on U.S. Treasury securities with a maturity date commensurate with the expected term of the associated award. The expected dividend yield is assumed to be </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'eb3-6f5-c89-8ba-f36b'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsWeightedAverageExpectedDividend" contextRef="D20260331" unitRef="USD" decimals="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="Tag441">zero</ix:nonFraction></span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> as the Company has never paid dividends and has no current plans to pay any dividends on its common stock. The assumptions used in calculating the fair value of share-based awards represent management&#8217;s best estimates and involve inherent uncertainties and the application of significant judgment.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Compensation expense for restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) with only service-based vesting conditions is recognized on a straight-line basis over the vesting period. Compensation cost for service-based RSUs is based on the grant date fair value of the award, which is the closing market price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date multiplied by the number of shares awarded.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">For awards that vest upon a liquidity event or a change in control, the performance condition is not probable of being achieved until the event occurs. As a result, no compensation expense is recognized until the performance-based vesting condition is achieved, at which time the cumulative compensation expense is recognized. Compensation cost related to any remaining time-based service for share-based awards after the liquidity-based event is recognized on a straight-line basis over the remaining service period.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">For fully vested, nonforfeitable equity instruments that are granted at the date the Company and a nonemployee enter into an agreement for goods or services, the Company recognizes the fair value of the equity instruments on the grant date. The corresponding cost is recognized as an immediate expense or a prepaid asset and expensed over the service period depending on the specific facts and circumstances of the agreement with the nonemployee. See Note </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c7c93237c1946f635b03'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">10</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> for further details.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c8b1ac81b7bf3b856ef3'"><ix:exclude><ix:exclude><p style="margin-top:0pt; See Note </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c8dbf1260408b95c5a15'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">12</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'b58-716-f7b-33e-6c0c'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag606"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; text-decoration:underline; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Recently Adopted and Issued Accounting Pronouncements</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">From time to time, the FASB issues Accounting Standards Updates (&#8220;ASUs&#8221;) to amend the authoritative literature in the ASC. Other than the pronouncements listed below, the Company believes that those issued to date either (i) provide supplemental guidance, (ii) are technical corrections, or (iii) are not applicable to the Company&#8217;s consolidated condensed financial statements or related disclosures.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after December </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c4227d4f684c80f6fc7b'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">15</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cdb1897f2589fc5290f5'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2026</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that ASU </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd9fcbee88c447594d3d'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">2024</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">-</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cea1fdf602d68e8ea393'; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">03</span></span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> will have on its financial statement disclosures.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06, </span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> (&#8220;ASU 2025-06&#8221;), which amends certain aspects of the accounting for and disclosure of software costs under ASC 350-40. The amendments modernize the recognition and disclosure framework for internal-use software costs, removing the previous &#8220;development stage&#8221; model and introducing a more judgment-based approach. The ASU is effective for all entities for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that ASU 2025-06 will have on its financial statements.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-07, </span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Derivatives Scope Refinements and Scope Clarification for Share-Based Noncash Consideration from a Customer in a Revenue Contract </span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">(&#8220;ASU 2025-07&#8221;)</span><span style="font-style:italic; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">.</span><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;"> ASU 2025-07 adds a new scope exception from derivative accounting under ASC 815 for certain non-exchange-traded contracts with customers with an underlying that is based on operations or activities specific to one of the parties to the contract. Further, ASU 2025-07 clarifies that an entity should apply the guidance in ASC 606 to a contract with stock-based noncash consideration. The ASU is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026 and interim periods within those annual periods, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact that ASU 2025-07 will have on its financial statements.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation></div><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_1328dfef6f0a0aa4'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">13</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_17"><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c51d122b5f22834151d0'"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:InventoryDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="D20260331" escape="true" id="Tag618"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">3. font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">Upon consummation of the IPO, the Company concluded that the contingent milestone payment is a freestanding financial instrument that meets the definition of a derivative under ASC 815, and accordingly, the fair value of the derivative liability is marked to market each reporting period until settled. The Royalty due to Knight was determined to be an embedded component of the Series A Preferred Stock, however, is exempt from derivative accounting under the ASC 815 scope exception for specified volumes of sales or service revenues. Therefore, the Company accrues a royalty expense as sales are made.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The Company uses a probability-weighted expected return method to determine the fair value of the contingent milestone payment. The valuation model uses significant unobservable inputs (Level 3), incorporating management&#8217;s assumptions regarding the timing and probability of discrete potential exit scenarios, forward interest rate curves, and a weighted average cost of capital based on implied and market yields to discount expected cash flows.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">The valuation of the contingent milestone payment requires significant judgment and is sensitive to changes in assumptions related to the expected timing of payment, the likelihood of potential exit scenarios, and the selected discount rate. In developing these assumptions, management considers various qualitative and quantitative factors, including the anticipated progression toward clinical, commercial, and profitability milestones and the potential for a strategic transaction following achievement of each milestone. These factors are evaluated collectively to assess the probability&#8209;weighted timing of the contingent payment under each potential exit scenario reflected in the valuation. Foreign sales to both Australia and Europe are further subject to profit sharing agreements for boxes sold to customers. Sales to resellers in the US are subject to considerable discounts and rebates for services provided by our third-party logistics (&#8220;3PL&#8221;) partner and wholesalers and pharmacy benefit managers (&#8220;PBMs&#8221;). We recognize revenue when control of Arakoda transfers to our U.S. distributor or 3PL partner, which generally occurs upon shipment. We record product revenue net of estimated discounts, rebates, chargebacks and product returns in accordance with ASC 606. We estimate these forms of variable consideration using the expected value method and constrain estimates to amounts for which it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue will not occur when the related uncertainties are resolved.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Cost of Revenues, Gross Profit, and Gross Margin</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Cost of revenues associated with our products is primarily comprised of direct materials, shipping, manufacturing-related costs incurred in the production process, serialization costs, and inventory write-downs due to expiration.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Other Operating Revenues</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Other operating revenues for the periods presented include research revenue earned from the Australian Tax Authority for research activities conducted in Australia. In 2025, other operating revenues also included research revenues associated with our contract with the United States Army Medical Material Development Activity (USAMMDA) for Arakoda supply chain upgrade support. We recognized research revenue related to the USAMMDA contract over time as qualifying costs were incurred, up to the maximum contractual funding amount. All funded activities under this contract were completed and fully reimbursed by December 31, 2025, and no additional amounts are expected to be earned under the arrangement. </span><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Operating Expenses</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Research and Development</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Research and development costs for the periods presented primarily consist of contracted research and development services and costs associated with preparation for and conducting our Babesiosis trial. We expense all research and development costs in the period in which they are incurred. Payments made prior to the receipt of goods or services to be used in research and development are recognized as prepaid assets and expensed over the service period as the services are provided. We have also issued shares of our common stock to vendors in exchange for research and development services.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">General and Administrative Expenses</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Our general and administrative expenses primarily consist of salaries, advertising and promotion expenses, professional services fees, such as consulting, audit, accounting and legal fees, general corporate costs and allocated costs, including facilities, information technology and amortization of intangibles.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Interest and Other Income, Net</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We earn interest income from cash invested in interest-bearing accounts, as well as cash equivalents and short-term investments consisting of certificates of deposits with original maturities ranging from three to six months. Interest expense for the periods presented is limited to a single $150,000 SBA loan that bears interest at 3.75%. The </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c59b7037d2c60fddf9b9'; -aw-sdt-title:'financing activities Direction'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">increase</span></span><span> in net cash provided by financing activities is attributable to higher net proceeds from the sale of common stock under our At-the-Market (ATM) Sales Agreement between January and March 2026, which exceeded the aggregate net proceeds of $</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'0a1-798-b16-25d-52f8'; -aw-sdt-title:'YTD 2025 Offering Proceeds SCF'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">1,712,973</span></span><span> received from our common stock and warrant offerings completed in January and February 2025. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>The increase was partially offset by lower proceeds from warrant exercises, which were $</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'ae6-101-a5d-1d6-cfb3'; -aw-sdt-title:'2026 Warrant Proceeds_SCF'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">0</span></span><span> for the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cb7bee36903057f67fc2'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current _Quarter._P48'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">three months ended March 31, 2026</span></span><span>, compared to $</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'678-582-a50-438-4213'; -aw-sdt-title:'2025 Warrant Proceeds_SCF'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">1,926</span></span><span> for the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c5be0befd84cfd940279'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous _Quarter._P34'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">three months ended March 31, 2025</span></span><span>. In addition, during the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'252-ccc-a8e-cc2-3177'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous _Quarter._P11'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">three months ended March 31, 2025</span></span><span>, we withheld shares valued at $</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'a90-d2a-3e4-b92-c23a'; -aw-sdt-title:'Share Settled Bonus PYTD_SCF'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">18,000</span></span><span> to cover tax withholdings associated with the net share settlement of certain 2024 performance bonuses awarded to our executives. No such share withholding or net share settlement activity occurred during the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c1baa1e646b390cc3645'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current _Quarter._P49'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">three months ended March 31, 2026</span></span><span>.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Effect of Foreign Currency Translation on Cash </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Our foreign operations were small relative to U.S. operations for the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c9e1684ce3fbb1eb992a'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current _Quarter._P50'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">three months ended March 31, 2026</span></span><span> and </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c4eee3a6d3a250762eb0'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous_Period_P4'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2025</span></span><span>, thus effects of foreign currency translation have been minor.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold">Critical Accounting Policies, Significant Judgments, and Use of Estimates</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Revenue Recognition </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We recognize revenue in accordance with FASB ASC Topic No. 606, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</span><span> (&#8220;ASC 606&#8221;). Revenues are recognized when control is transferred to customers in amounts that reflect the consideration we expect to be entitled to receive in exchange for those goods. Revenue recognition is evaluated through the following five steps: (i) identification of the contract, or contracts, with a customer; (ii) identification of the performance obligations in the contract; (iii) determination of the transaction price; (iv) allocation of the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v) recognition of revenue when or as a performance obligation is satisfied. As part of the accounting for these arrangements, we may be required to make significant judgments, including identifying performance obligations in the contract, estimating the amount of variable consideration to include in the transaction price and allocating the transaction price to each performance obligation.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_c201c8d26e01a0f0276b'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">32</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_36"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Revenues from product sales are recorded at the net sales price, or &#8220;transaction price,&#8221; which may include estimates of variable consideration that result from product returns. We determine the amount of variable consideration by using either the expected value method or the most-likely-amount method. We include the unconstrained amount of estimated variable consideration in the transaction price, which reflects the amount for which it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur. At the end of each subsequent reporting period, we re-evaluate the estimated variable consideration included in the transaction price and any related constraint, and if necessary, adjust our estimate of the overall transaction price. Any such adjustments are recorded on a cumulative catch-up basis in the period of adjustment. Reserves are established for the estimates of variable consideration based on the amounts we expect to be earned or to be claimed on the related sales.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We record U.S. commercial revenues as a receivable when our American distributor transfers shipped product to their title model for 60P. Foreign sales to both Australia and Europe are recognized as a receivable at the point product is shipped to distributor. The shipments to Australia and Europe were further subject to profit sharing agreements for boxes sold to customers.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Inventory </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We report inventories at the lower of cost or net realizable value. Cost is comprised of direct materials and, where applicable, costs we incur in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition. We use the Specific Identification method per lot. A box or a bottle price is calculated per lot number and sales are recognized by their lot number. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We regularly monitor our inventory levels to identify inventory that may expire or has a cost basis in excess of its estimated realizable value, and record write-downs for inventory that has expired, inventory that has a cost basis in excess of its expected net realizable value, and inventory in excess of expected sales requirements. We charge any write-downs of inventories to Cost of Revenues in the Consolidated Condensed Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Loss.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Share-Based Payments</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We account for share-based payments in accordance with ASC Subtopic 718, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Compensation - Stock Compensation</span><span> (&#8220;ASC 718&#8221;). We measure compensation for all share-based payment awards granted to employees, directors, and nonemployees, based on the estimated fair value of the awards on the date of grant. For awards that vest based on continued service, the service-based compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period of the awards. For service vesting awards with compensation expense recognized on a straight-line basis, at no point in time does the cumulative grant date value of vested awards exceed the cumulative amount of compensation expense recognized. The grant date is determined based on the date when a mutual understanding of the key terms of the share-based awards is established. We account for forfeitures as they occur.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We estimate the fair value of all stock option awards as of the grant date by applying the Black-Scholes option pricing model. The application of this valuation model involves assumptions, including the fair value of the common stock, expected volatility, risk-free interest rate, expected dividends and the expected term of the option. Due to the lack of a public market for our common stock prior to the IPO and lack of company-specific historical implied volatility data, we base our computations of expected volatility on the historical volatility of a representative group of public companies with similar characteristics of the Company, including stage of development and industry focus. The historical volatility is calculated based on a period of time commensurate with the expected term assumption. We generally use the simplified method as prescribed by the SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin Topic 14, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Share-Based Payment</span><span>, to estimate the expected term for stock options, whereby, the expected term equals the midpoint of the weighted average remaining time to vest, vesting period and the contractual term of the options due to our lack of historical exercise data. For certain options granted out-of-the-money, our best estimate of the expected term is the contractual term of the award. The risk-free interest rate is based on U.S. Treasury securities with a maturity date commensurate with the expected term of the associated award. The expected dividend yield is assumed to be zero as we have never paid dividends and have no current plans to pay any dividends on our common stock. The assumptions used in calculating the fair value of share-based awards represent our best estimates and involve inherent uncertainties and the application of significant judgment.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We recognize compensation expense for restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;) with only service-based vesting conditions on a straight-line basis over the vesting period. Compensation cost for service-based RSUs is based on the grant date fair value of the award, which is the closing market price of our common stock on the grant date multiplied by the number of shares awarded.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>For awards that vest upon a liquidity event or a change in control, the performance condition is not probable of being achieved until the event occurs. As a result, no compensation expense is recognized until the performance-based vesting condition is achieved, at which time the cumulative compensation expense is recognized. Compensation cost related to any remaining time-based service for share-based awards after the liquidity-based event is recognized on a straight-line basis over the remaining service period.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_cf64678e6607e55488a8'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">33</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_37"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>For fully vested, nonforfeitable equity instruments that are granted at the date we enter into an agreement for goods or services with a nonemployee, we recognize the fair value of the equity instruments on the grant date. The corresponding cost is recognized as an immediate expense or a prepaid asset and expensed over the service period depending on the specific facts and circumstances of the agreement with the nonemployee.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Derivative Liabilities</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We assess the classification of our derivative financial instruments each reporting period, and determined that such instruments initially qualified for treatment as derivative liabilities as they met the criteria for liability classification under ASC 815. As of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c47da0b90c9365950a78'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P36'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span>, our derivative liabilities consist of contingent payment arrangements. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>We analyze all financial instruments with features of both liabilities and equity under the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) Topic No. 480, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity</span><span> (&#8220;ASC 480&#8221;) and FASB ASC Topic No. 815, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Derivatives and Hedging</span><span> (&#8220;ASC 815&#8221;). Derivative liabilities are adjusted to reflect fair value at each reporting period, with any increase or decrease in the fair value recorded in the results of operations, as a component of other income or expense as change in fair value of derivative liabilities. We use a probability-weighted expected return method to determine the fair value of these instruments.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Upon conversion or repayment of a debt or equity instrument in exchange for equity shares, where the embedded conversion option has been bifurcated and accounted for as a derivative liability (generally convertible debt and warrants), we record the equity shares at fair value on the date of conversion, relieve all related debt, derivative liabilities, and unamortized debt discounts, and recognize a net gain or loss on debt extinguishment, if any.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Equity or liability instruments that become subject to reclassification under ASC Topic 815 are reclassified at the fair value of the instrument on the reclassification date.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>During 2026 and 2025, we did not have any relationships with unconsolidated organizations or financial partnerships, such as structured finance or special purpose entities that would have been established for the purpose of facilitating off-balance sheet arrangements or other contractually narrow or limited purposes.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">JOBS Act Accounting Election</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>In April 2012, the JOBS Act was enacted. Section 107(b) of the JOBS Act provides that an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; can take advantage of the extended transition period provided in Section 7(a)(2)(B) of the Securities Act for complying with new or revised accounting standards. Thus, an emerging growth company can delay the adoption of certain accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. We have elected to avail ourselves of this exemption and, therefore, we will not be subject to the same new or revised accounting standards as other public companies that are not emerging growth companies.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold; font-style:italic">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>From time to time, the FASB issues Accounting Standards Updates (&#8220;ASUs&#8221;) to amend the authoritative literature in the ASC. We regularly evaluate new ASUs to determine the impact that these pronouncements may have on our consolidated condensed financial statements. Other than the pronouncements listed below, management believes that those issued to date either (i) provide supplemental guidance, (ii) are technical corrections, or (iii) are not applicable to our consolidated condensed financial statements or related disclosures.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_cdb14d6e35d84660165b'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">34</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_38"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</span><span> (&#8220;ASU 2024-03&#8221;), which applies to all public business entities that file financial statements with the SEC. The amendments in this ASU require public business entities to disclose on an annual and interim basis, disaggregated information about certain income statement expense line items. The new standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2026, with early adoption permitted. We are currently evaluating the impact that ASU 2024-03 will have on our financial statement disclosures.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Intangibles - Goodwill and Other - Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software</span><span> (&#8220;ASU 2025-06&#8221;), which amends certain aspects of the accounting for and disclosure of software costs under ASC 350-40. The amendments modernize the recognition and disclosure framework for internal-use software costs, removing the previous &#8220;development stage&#8221; model and introducing a more judgment-based approach. The ASU is effective for all entities for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027, with early adoption permitted. We are currently evaluating the impact that ASU 2025-06 will have on our financial statements. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-07, </span><span style="font-style:italic">Derivatives Scope Refinements and Scope Clarification for Share-Based Noncash Consideration from a Customer in a Revenue Contract</span><span> (&#8220;ASU 2025-07&#8221;). ASU 2025-07 adds a new scope exception from derivative accounting under ASC 815 for certain non-exchange-traded contracts with customers with an underlying that is based on operations or activities specific to one of the parties to the contract. Further, ASU 2025-07 clarifies that an entity should apply the guidance in ASC 606 to a contract with stock-based noncash consideration. The ASU is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026 and interim periods within those annual periods, with early adoption permitted. We are currently evaluating the impact that ASU 2025-07 will have on our financial statements.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-weight:bold">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><a id="TOC_c048e7bcdce9d8c360e2" href="#"></a><span style="font-weight:bold">ITEM 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span></span><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>As a smaller reporting company as defined by Rule 12b-2 of the Exchange Act of 1934, as amended and in Item 10(f)(1) of Regulation S-K, we are electing scaled disclosure reporting obligations and therefore are not required to provide the information requested by this item.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><a id="TOC_c44a338213ccfed10dc0" href="#"></a><span style="font-weight:bold">ITEM 4. Controls and Procedures. Disclosure Controls and Procedures </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span></span><span style="font-weight:bold">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, have evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'cd1dab4fa21277f32620'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P34'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span>. Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer have concluded that as of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c8278e2de05d7e0fa07a'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P35'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span>, due to the existence of the material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting described below, our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over our financial reporting, as such term is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act. Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. Our management has used the framework set forth in the report entitled &#8220;Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013)&#8221; published by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission to evaluate the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting. </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>Based on this assessment, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c52cb02cdd6098cc3f36'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P33'"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">March 31, 2026</span></span><span>, due to the existence of material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting. These material weaknesses are described below: </span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt; font-size:10pt"><span>(1)</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:justify; font-size:10pt"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Inadequate Design of Policies and Procedures</span><span>: We did not design policies and procedures at a sufficient level of precision to support the operating effectiveness of controls to prevent and detect potential errors.</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:0pt;
